uncited: Upsampling and Super-Resolution methods in volume rendering address the problem of increasing the spatial resolution of volumetric data or rendered images to recover fine details, correct discrete positioning errors, or optimize rendering performance.

This family is distinguished from sibling multiresolution techniques (which often focus on downsampling or LOD selection for culling) by its primary goal of generating higher-fidelity representations from lower-resolution inputs, either through geometric remapping, interpolation, or learning-based refinement.
The core mechanism across these methods involves expanding the spatial domain of a volume or image.
The concept of upsampling in volumetric data is rooted in the need to mitigate aliasing and improve the perceptual quality of synthesized views.

This directly supports the claim that discrete domain positioning errors lead to poor subjective quality when the volume is not fine enough, motivating the use of double-resolution pre-processing.
